heading: Which languages can I use?
summary: You can write a Tac service in the supported languages below. Lua, Python and C++ are supported with limits. Other WebAssembly languages are not supported.
body:
A Tac service is a class in `client/services`. Tachyon reads that class, connects its fields, methods, events and storage to the page, and runs its test units. A language is a Tac service language only when Tachyon does all of this for it. A compiler that makes WebAssembly is not enough. Each language below is in one of four groups.

Supported and tested: JavaScript and TypeScript run in the page as JavaScript. Rust, Go, C#, F#, Swift, Kotlin, Java, Dart and Ruby run in the page as WebAssembly. Tachyon tests each of these languages with its own test units and in a real browser. The feature pages show examples in them, and the site build checks those examples. When one of these languages cannot use a feature, the feature page says so and names the build error.

Supported with limits: Lua, Python and C++ work, but some features are not ready in them yet. Each feature page says when Lua, Python or C++ cannot use the feature.

Lua runs on Tachyon's Lua 5.4 WebAssembly runtime (ADR 0085; an ADR is an architecture decision record). A Lua service has fields, methods, `OnStart` and `OnStop`, events with `ApplicationEventPublisher` and `OnEvent`, topics, delegates, the behavior annotations, `Store`, `HTTPClient`, `LocalState` and `SessionState` fields, test units, and Tachyon's browser APIs except `WindowControls` and `FilePicker`. A `WindowControls` or `FilePicker` field in a Lua service stops the build with `TY2015`.

Python runs on Pyodide 314.0.7, a Python runtime for WebAssembly (ADR 0093). A Python service has fields, methods, `async def` methods, models, `Needs`, `NeedsAll`, `Named`, delegates, `LocalState` and `SessionState` fields, the behavior annotations, `Store`, `HTTPClient`, `Converter`, `on_start` (plain or `async def`), plain `on_stop` and `on_event` methods, an `ApplicationEventPublisher` field, topics and test units. The page gets a promise for an `async def` method, which runs as an asyncio task and can await helpers and `asyncio.sleep`. Other calls run while it waits. Disposing the service cancels its waiting tasks and rejects their promises with `CANCELLED`. A Python `HTTPClient` may carry `StreamRequest` and `SocketRequest`: the page holds the connection for the service that keeps the client in a `Needs` field, and a socket client gets `async def send(self, message)`. An `async def` `on_stop` or `on_event`, or a browser API, stops the build with `TY1605`. ADR 0093 covers web builds; Tachyon does not test Python services in native apps.

C++ runs as WebAssembly that Emscripten builds from header-only `.hpp` files, one class in each file (ADR 0099). A C++ service has fields, methods, `Needs`, `NeedsAll`, `Named`, `Lifetime` (`singleton` or `prototype`), `OnStart` and `OnStop`, events with `ApplicationEventPublisher` and `OnEvent` (with `Order` and `InBackground`), `LocalState` and `SessionState` fields, models in `client/models` (also `Checked`, `Settings` and `Topic` models), `HTTPClient` clients in `client/remotes`, delegates, converters, and test units. A synchronous service method may carry `Cached`, `UpdateCache`, `ClearCache`, `Retry`, `MaxAtOnce`, `AllOrNothing` and a `PageDefaults` parameter. A `Store` with its `Entity` keeps its rows in IndexedDB. A method that returns `Task<T>` is awaited by the page. A C++ `HTTPClient` may carry `StreamRequest` and `SocketRequest`: the page holds the connection for the service that keeps the client in a `Needs` field, and a socket client gets `Task<void> send(message)`. A C++ `Setup` in client/setups gives a client its HTTP adapter and a Store its entity adapter. `Cached`, `Retry` and the other behavior markers go on synchronous and `Task` service methods, and a C++ `HTTPClient` method takes `Cached`, `UpdateCache` and `ClearCache`. A `Needs` field may also name one of Tachyon's browser APIs, such as `[[Needs]] Clock& clock;`, and a call that the page refuses throws a `std::runtime_error`. A C++ test unit uses `Fake`, `ValueSource` and HTTP answers from its TestSetup, and `ty test --coverage` records the C++ methods that each case runs. C++ links into no native host. In Yon, C++ has controllers, services, delegates, converters, workers, setups, checked models, caching, retries, transactions and stores so far.

In progress and planned: you cannot use these languages today, and the plan can change. Zig is planned. Scala, through the WebAssembly output of Scala.js, and MoonBit, after its version 1.0, are under consideration.

Not supported: many other languages can reach a browser through WebAssembly, for example Haskell, OCaml, Grain, Nim, D, Odin, Crystal, AssemblyScript, Elixir, PHP, Perl and R. Tachyon does not support them as Tac service languages, and you cannot write a Tac service in them. Some languages compile to JavaScript, not to WebAssembly, for example Gleam, Elm and ClojureScript. Tachyon does not support them as Tac service languages either. A server language such as PHP can still be a Yon language (see The Yon languages).

The first table shows how each language runs and which tools build it.

| Language | Runs as | Toolchain |
| --- | --- | --- |
| JavaScript | JavaScript in the page | none |
| TypeScript | JavaScript in the page, after `tsc` | TypeScript 6 or newer |
| Rust | WebAssembly (`wasm32-unknown-unknown`) | rustc 1.97.1 |
| Go | WebAssembly (`GOOS=js GOARCH=wasm`) | Go 1.27 or newer; TinyGo 0.42 or newer is optional and makes release modules smaller |
| C# | WebAssembly on the trimmed .NET browser runtime | .NET SDK 9.0.317 (`net9.0`) with the `wasm-tools` workload |
| F# | WebAssembly on the same .NET browser runtime as C# | the same .NET SDK as C# |
| Swift | WebAssembly (`wasm32-unknown-wasip1`) | Swift 6.3.3 from swift.org and its Swift SDK for WebAssembly, found through `TAC_SWIFT_WASM_SDK` |
| Kotlin | WebAssembly with garbage collection (WasmGC) | kotlinc 2.1.10 and kotlin-stdlib-wasm-js 2.1.10, found through `TAC_KOTLIN_WASM_STDLIB` |
| Java | WasmGC, made by TeaVM | JDK 21 or newer and TeaVM 0.15.0 |
| Dart | WasmGC (`dart compile wasm`) | Dart SDK 3.13 or newer |
| Ruby | Tachyon's mruby WebAssembly runtime | Ruby and Emscripten 6.0.10 build the pinned mruby once on your machine |
| Lua (with limits) | Tachyon's Lua 5.4.9 WebAssembly runtime, about 170 KB | Emscripten 6.0.10 builds it once on your machine |
| Python (with limits) | Pyodide 314.0.7 (CPython 3.14.2), about 13 MB before compression | the five pinned Pyodide files, which you put in the Tachyon cache |
| C++ (with limits) | WebAssembly, compiled by Emscripten | Emscripten 6.0.10 (`em++`) |

The second table shows how each language behaves. Calls says whether the page waits for a method. Native host says where a native app links the service in; everywhere else the service runs in the page, also inside a native app. `HTTPClient` says how a client in that language sends requests (see Calling the server from a page). Example names a working service in Code examples on the home page; the site build compiles and checks each one.

| Language | Calls | Native host | HTTPClient | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| JavaScript | Synchronous or `async` | none | sent by the browser | `TallyService.js` |
| TypeScript | Synchronous or `async` | none | sent by the browser | `TallyService.ts` |
| Rust | Synchronous; an `async fn` runs on Tachyon's task runner in the module | macOS, Windows, Linux and iOS | sent by the browser, through `Needs` | `TallyService.rs` |
| Go | Each call runs in a goroutine; a call that waits finishes later | none | sent by the browser, through `Needs` | `TallyService.go` |
| C# | Synchronous; a `Task` method is awaited | Windows | sent by the browser, through `Needs` | `TallyService.cs` |
| F# | Synchronous; a `Task` method is awaited | none | sent by the browser | `TallyService.fs` |
| Swift | Synchronous; an `async` method runs as a task in the module and the page gets a promise (in a native app it runs to the end before the call returns) | macOS and iOS | sent by the browser, through `Needs` | `TallyService.swift` |
| Kotlin | Synchronous; a `suspend fun` waits in the module and the page gets a promise | Android | sent by the browser, through `Needs` | `TallyService.kt` |
| Java | Each call runs in a TeaVM fiber; a call that waits finishes later | none | sent by the browser, through `Needs` | `TallyService.java` |
| Dart | Synchronous; a `Future` method is awaited | none | sent by the browser, through `Needs` | `TallyService.dart` |
| Ruby | Each call runs in a Ruby fiber; a call that waits finishes later; `sleep` is refused | none | sent by the browser, through `Needs` | `TallyService.rb` |
| Lua | Synchronous | none | sent by the browser, through `Needs` | `TallyService.lua` |
| Python | Synchronous; an `async def` method runs as an asyncio task and the page gets a promise | none | sent by the browser, through `Needs` | `TallyService.py` |
| C++ | Synchronous; a `Task<T>` method is awaited | none | sent by the browser, through `Needs` | `TallyService.hpp` |

Kotlin, Java and Dart need a browser with WasmGC: Chrome or Edge 119, Firefox 120, Safari 18.2 or newer. Java also needs WebAssembly exception references (exnref): Chrome or Edge 137, Firefox 131, Safari 18.4 or newer. Dart also needs the JavaScript exception tag (`WebAssembly.JSTag`): Chrome or Edge 119, Firefox 131, Safari 18.4 or newer. An older browser shows a clear error instead of these services. `ty doctor` lists the tools that your project needs and says which ones are missing. A page loads the runtime of a language only when one of its views uses a service in that language.
